title: "Reproducible analysis" module (literate programming, seeds, pinning)
context: Ad-hoc analysis scripts with no seed setting, unpinned dependencies, and no literate programming account for a large share of unreproducible cancer findings. This module teaches literate programming (Quarto, R Markdown, Jupyter), random-seed setting, and dependency pinning using a CI-rendered runnable example. Because a real open cancer dataset is used for the worked example (requiring a committed PASS gate artifact from datagate-002), this task is risk tier medium. Depends on: template-004, container-ci-005, datagate-002.
objective: Author the 'Reproducible analysis' module covering literate programming (Quarto/R Markdown/Jupyter), seed setting, and dependency pinning, with a runnable CI-rendered worked example on an open cancer dataset that has a committed PASS gate artifact; all assertions cited; CI green; signed off by Educator, Data & licensing, and Technical reviewers.
acceptanceCriteria: Module follows the template: 3-6 Bloom-aligned learning objectives, lesson narrative with all assertions cited, runnable pinned-container exercise, CI-rendered worked example, checklist/takeaway, formative assessment, and instructor notes.

Teaches literate programming (Quarto, R Markdown, and/or Jupyter notebooks), random-seed setting (set.seed / numpy.random.seed / torch.manual_seed), and dependency pinning (conda lockfile, renv, or pip requirements pinned to exact versions).

Worked example uses a real open cancer dataset with a committed PASS gate artifact (datagate-002 criteria: permitsDerivatives: true, non-identifiable); data fetched at runtime in bounded slices; no raw data committed.

Example is purely methodological — it teaches how to make the analysis reproducible, presents no biological/clinical conclusion as a finding, and is labeled 'teaching example — not a finding, not advice.'
Worked example renders successfully in CI (Quarto render or papermill); container builds and passes smoke test (Docker + Apptainer); link/citation checker passes.
Reviewed and signed off by Educator reviewer, Data & licensing reviewer, and Technical reviewer; DCO signed off.
resources: The Turing Way — reproducible environments chapter
DepMap (CC-BY 4.0, https://depmap.org/portal/) or GDC open-tier as example dataset
output: A complete 'Reproducible analysis' module committed to the project repo (lesson, CI-rendered worked example with PASS gate artifact, exercise, checklist, assessment, instructor notes), with CI green (Docker + Apptainer) and Educator + Data & licensing + Technical reviewer sign-offs.
